policy.purpose: Authoritative suspend/resume resilience inventory for managed AQ-OS workloads. A workload must be registered before it may claim suspend-safe operation.
policy.scope: Managed long-running AI workloads and resumable development jobs. This v1 inventory is deliberately bounded; it is not a claim that every repository script is suspend-safe.
policy.registration_rule: New managed long-running workloads must add an AQ_SUSPEND_CONTRACT marker and a matching record in the same slice that introduces their service, timer, or resumable job entrypoint.
policy.out_of_scope: Two classes of systemd unit are deliberately NOT registered as managed workloads because they have no long-running or suspend/resume semantics: (1) disposable test-only VM hosts (nix/hosts/aqos-vm, nix/hosts/aqos-install-vm) declare fire-once Type=oneshot boot-marker services (e.g. aqos-install-vm-dogfood-marker, aqos-install-vm-ai-dev-factory-topology) that print a boot marker and exit; (2) periodic timer-driven health/monitor oneshots that fire, run one read-only check, write a status file, and exit (e.g. disk-health-monitor, fast-lane-staleness-monitor) - a timer re-runs them, there is no in-flight state to suspend/resume.

state_safety.idempotency: A stateless inference daemon may be restarted; in-flight requests must tolerate interruption.

workloads.next_slice: SR-3 resume reconciler emits typed outcome telemetry and supplies dashboard plus live QA parity.

state_safety.idempotency: Each completed training item is recorded before the next item is started.
state_safety.signal_behavior: SIGTERM and SIGHUP preserve progress for a later resume.

workloads.next_slice: SR-3 reconciler should make checkpoint recovery observable and bounded after a system resume.

state_safety.idempotency: A future resume must reconcile the existing run ledger before it dispatches another task.
state_safety.signal_behavior: Current bounded cancellation is not a checkpoint/resume guarantee.

workloads.next_slice: SR-4 adds signal-safe checkpointing, --resume, typed outcomes, and live evidence.
